answer.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding-simplification test is the intervention most likely to move both and to compound into sustainable qualified revenue. It is also the direction with the most convergent inherited support: memory_86 (onboarding shortening lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (field reduction gave a durable first-week activation lift) point the same way, with memory_91 suggesting activation messaging as a complementary follow-on rather than this week's slot. Promotional pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is explicitly caveated: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact, and discount-led acquisition of price-sensitive SMBs is exactly the kind of revenue that can be low-retention and margin-eroding under a long-term qualified-revenue objective. That is why I spend one verification pull on memory_73 (to see whether the flaw is fatal or merely noisy, which determines whether pricing stays a live option next cycle) and one on memory_86 (the most recent and most load-bearing claim for the action I actually intend, since I have not yet seen whether its lift was in completion only or carried through to retained, qualified accounts). Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) are plausible but address neither of the observed declines and referrals depend on an established base that a weakening activation funnel is not currently replenishing. Downstream value risk is flagged in both directions: cutting signup fields can strip qualification data and admit lower-intent accounts that inflate activation while degrading pipeline quality, so success criteria should be retained qualified accounts at 30-60 days, not completion rate alone, and the enterprise demo-request path from memory_44 should be preserved rather than collapsed into the simplified flow. Uncertainty is preserved: all six memories are archived summaries whose original effect sizes, durations, and segment definitions I have not inspected, the inherited lifts were measured in a pre-competitor market that may no longer hold, and none of them were tested against a declining baseline like the current one. I therefore run this at standard experiment scale with a holdout and segment-level readout rather than broad rollout, and I will revise if the memory_86 record shows the lift was completion-only or short-lived.
